subject: Physical Sciences
pacing_note: The IEB publishes no ATP equivalent; term placement and week spans are the DBE ATP pacing carried over as a default. IEB schools set their own pacing — treat weeks as advisory.
assessment_note: DBE SBA programmes, control-test scopes and exam structures are deliberately stripped: IEB assessment is specified by the IEB Subject Assessment Guidelines (see ../exam_guidelines/), which have not been ingested yet. Do not fall back to the CAPS exam_structure for IEB papers.
scope_deltas: SAG-stated content-scope differences vs the CAPS/DBE prescription are recorded in scope_deltas.json in this folder (hand-maintained, SAG-transcribed only; an empty ledger means 'not yet transcribed', never 'no differences').

topics.name: WAVES, SOUND AND LIGHT: Transverse pulses on a string, spring
subtopics: Pulse, transverse pulse and amplitude
Principle of superposition; constructive and destructive interference of pulses

topics.name: WAVES, SOUND AND LIGHT: Transverse waves
subtopics: Transverse wave; wavelength, frequency, period, amplitude, crest, trough
Points in phase and out of phase
f = 1/T and the wave equation v = fλ in problems

topics.name: WAVES, SOUND AND LIGHT: Longitudinal waves
subtopics: Longitudinal wave in a spring; compression and rarefaction
Wavelength, amplitude, period and frequency of longitudinal waves
Differentiate longitudinal vs transverse waves; v = fλ problems

topics.name: WAVES, SOUND AND LIGHT: Sound
subtopics: Sound as a longitudinal wave; wave speed vs properties of the medium
Echoes; v = fλ problems including sonar, bats, dolphins
Pitch vs frequency; loudness vs amplitude and ear sensitivity; quality vs waveform
Ultrasound (20–100 kHz); ultrasound imaging and medical uses

topics.name: WAVES, SOUND AND LIGHT: Electromagnetic radiation
subtopics: Wave model vs particle model of electromagnetic radiation
Source and propagation of EM waves; c = 3×10⁸ m·s⁻¹
EM spectrum ordered by frequency/wavelength; a use per radiation type
c = fλ calculations
Penetrating ability vs energy; dangers of gamma rays, X-rays and UV
Photon; photon energy E = hf = hc/λ

topics.name: ELECTRICITY AND MAGNETISM: Electrostatics
subtopics: Positive and negative charge; neutral vs charged objects
Tribo-electric charging of insulators
SI unit of charge; conservation of charge, Q = (Q1+Q2)/2 for identical charges
Charge quantization Q = nq
Like charges repel, opposite attract; polarization of insulators

topics.name: ELECTRICITY AND MAGNETISM: Electric circuits
subtopics: Potential difference V = W/Q; emf and terminal potential difference
Current I = Q/Δt; the coulomb; conventional current direction
Connecting and reading an ammeter and a voltmeter
Resistance: definition, microscopic description; effect of temperature, length, thickness

topics.name: CONTROL TEST: Discussion and remedial work
ELECTRICITY AND MAGNETISM: Electric circuits
subtopics: Energy transformations in a battery and resistors (why a battery goes flat)
Series circuits: same current, potential-difference dividers, Rs = R1 + R2 + …
Parallel circuits: same potential difference, current dividers, 1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + …

topics.name: MATTER AND MATERIAL: States of matter and the kinetic molecular theory
subtopics: Particle nature of matter; diffusion and Brownian motion
Material properties: strength, brittle/malleable/ductile, density, melting and boiling points
Mixture, pure substance, element, compound
Three states of matter; freezing, melting and boiling points
Heating and cooling curves; identify state at a given temperature
Changes of state: melting, evaporation, freezing, sublimation, condensation
Solid, liquid, gas in terms of the Kinetic Molecular Theory

topics.name: MATTER AND MATERIAL: The atom
subtopics: Atomic structure: nucleus and surrounding electrons
Atomic number, protons, electrons, neutrons, mass number; ion charges
Isotopes; relative atomic mass from isotope percentages
Element notation (A over Z next to symbol)
Aufbau diagrams and sp notation up to Z = 20
Atomic orbitals and their energies

topics.name: MATTER AND MATERIAL: Periodic table
subtopics: Names and formulae using the cation/anion table
Metals, non-metals, metalloids; electrical/thermal conductors, semiconductors, insulators; magnetic classification
Periodic table organisation by atomic number; group and period numbers; position vs electronic structure
Periodicity Li→Ar: atomic radius, ionisation energy, electron affinity, electronegativity
Chemical properties and reactivity trends of groups 1, 2, 17 and 18
Positions of metals, non-metals and transition metals

topics.name: MATTER AND MATERIAL: Chemical bonding
subtopics: Chemical bond; Lewis dot diagrams of elements
Covalent bonding: molecules, Lewis diagrams (H2, F2, Cl2, O2, N2, HF, HCl, CH4, NH3, H2O), names and formulae
Ionic bonding: formula-unit, cations and anions, Lewis diagrams (NaCl, KCl, KBr, CaCl2, MgBr2), predicting ions from the periodic table, naming
Metallic bonding
Relative molecular and formula mass calculations

topics.name: CHEMICAL CHANGE: Physical and chemical change
subtopics: Physical change vs chemical change, with examples

topics.name: CHEMICAL CHANGE: Representing chemical change
subtopics: Word equations ↔ chemical equations; phase indicators (s), (aq), (l), (g)
Balancing chemical equations; conservation of atoms and mass; law of constant composition

topics.name: CHEMICAL CHANGE: Quantitative aspects of chemical change
subtopics: The mole, Avogadro's number, molar mass
n = m/M calculations
Avogadro's law; molar gas volume at STP
Volume relationships in balanced gas equations

topics.name: CONTROL TEST: Discussion and remedial work
CHEMICAL CHANGE: Quantitative aspects of chemical change
subtopics: Concentration c = n/V (mol·dm⁻³)
Percentage composition; empirical formula from percentage composition
Water of crystallisation (e.g. CuSO4·5H2O)
Stoichiometric calculations from balanced equations (concentration, mass, moles, particles, volume)
Theoretical and percentage yield

topics.name: MECHANICS: Vectors and scalars
subtopics: Physical quantities; vector vs scalar
Graphical representation; equality of vectors, negative vectors, addition in one dimension
Resultant: tail-to-head method and by calculation (max four force vectors, 1D)

topics.name: MECHANICS: Motion in one dimension
subtopics: Frame of reference; position relative to a reference point
Distance vs displacement
Average speed and average velocity
Acceleration a = Δv/Δt; positive/negative acceleration vs deceleration

topics.name: MECHANICS: Instantaneous speed and velocity and the equations of motion
subtopics: Instantaneous velocity and instantaneous speed
Uniform velocity vs uniformly accelerated motion
Position-time, velocity-time and acceleration-time graphs: gradients, tangents, areas
Equations of motion in the horizontal plane; vehicle safety and stopping distance

topics.name: MECHANICS: Energy
subtopics: Gravitational potential energy Ep = mgh
Kinetic energy Ek = ½mv²

topics.name: SEPTEMBER CONTROL TEST: Discussion and remedial work
MECHANICS: Energy
subtopics: Mechanical energy EM = Ek + Ep
Law of conservation of energy; principle of conservation of mechanical energy
Apply conservation of mechanical energy: drops, vertical throws, pendulum, roller coasters, inclined planes
